author: Mark Atwood
text:
Investigated; this is a workspace-architectural release-process decision, not a single-crate code change. Filing 'human' so the next pass can pick one of three options that affect 30+ crates.

## State of affairs (verified 2026-05-16)

- jmap-mail-types Cargo.toml: `version = "0.1.1"`. Workspace Cargo.toml line 55-59 says: "Use version = '0.1' (caret-major) so any 0.1.x release of a sibling satisfies the constraint; bump to version = '0.2' workspace-wide when the coordinated 0.2 API-break beads (bd:JMAP-g7wu.1 CallerCtx, bd:JMAP-g7wu.3 helpers builder, bd:JMAP-g7wu.9 UTCDate, bd:JMAP-r3pg.14 extract_account_id) land together." All four named beads are now CLOSED (verified via `bd show`). The coordinated 0.2 bump is unblocked by its originally-listed prerequisites but has not been cut.
- Parallel evidence: JMAP-6xs8.3 (open, P1) is the jmap-types version of the same bead. JMAP-6xs8.22 (open, P2) asks for a CHANGELOG.md for jmap-types. JMAP-j7pa.2 (this bead) is the jmap-mail-types instance. No standalone 'cut the coordinated 0.2 release' bead exists yet.
- Across the 32 crates: 14 are at 0.1.1, 1 at 0.1.2 (jmap-mail-server, jmap-server), 4 at 0.1.0 (metadata + cid), testjig at 0.0.0. The workspace is already inconsistent on per-crate patch versions but has not been bumped for the 0.1→0.2 breaking shift the Cargo.toml comment anticipates.

## Three options I considered

(a) **Cut the coordinated 0.2 release now.** File a workspace-level epic that batches: bump every public crate's version to 0.2.0, update workspace.dependencies caret to '0.2', write a one-time CHANGELOG.md per crate covering all 0.1→0.2 breaks (CallerCtx, helpers builder, UTCDate newtype, extract_account_id reshape, MailboxFilterCondition.parent_id Option<Id>→Option<Value>, all the jmap-types extras/State changes). This is what the Cargo.toml comment plans for and now appears overdue. Closes JMAP-j7pa.2, JMAP-6xs8.3, JMAP-6xs8.22 as part of the cut.

(b) **Patch-bump jmap-mail-types alone (0.1.1 → 0.1.2) with a NOTES section** in a new CHANGELOG.md. Closes JMAP-j7pa.2 in isolation. Leaves JMAP-6xs8.3 / JMAP-6xs8.22 to do the same for jmap-types. Creates incoherent release timing across the workspace (downstream consumers pull a 0.1.2 jmap-mail-types that breaks against 0.1.1 jmap-mail-server unless that bumps too).

(c) **Defer.** Leave version at 0.1.1, accept that anyone pinning to ^0.1 on crates.io gets the breaking change silently, file a 'cut 0.2 by date X' bead for future scheduling. Pre-1.0 SemVer allows this; the workspace cookie-cutter comment implies it's the current status quo.

## Recommendation

Option (a). It's the path the Cargo.toml comment was already aiming at, all four originally-cited blockers are closed, and it's the cheapest way to resolve the three open beads (this one, 6xs8.3, 6xs8.22) plus any future ones of the same shape. Filing a new epic 'cut workspace 0.2 release' that consumes the three existing beads as children seems like the right shape.

Question for human: pick (a), (b), or (c). If (a), authorize me to file the epic and start work on it; that epic touches every crate's Cargo.toml + adds CHANGELOG.md to every published crate, which is a workspace-architectural mass change that I don't want to start without an explicit go.

Cross-refs: JMAP-6xs8.3, JMAP-6xs8.22, JMAP-g7wu.1, JMAP-g7wu.3, JMAP-g7wu.9, JMAP-r3pg.14.
